payload.channelWideVisualApproach: Cinematic historical-mystery animation for casual entertainment: preserve factual boundaries while turning people, danger, discovery, contradiction, and human reversal into an immediately readable chain of dramatic events.
realismAndFactualityPrinciples: Prefer historically plausible people, spaces, objects, materials, clothing, and environmental conditions unless an approved reconstruction mode explicitly authorizes fantasy stylization.
Do not present a generated reconstruction as authenticated primary evidence, an archival photograph, a map, a document, or an artifact.
When the script expresses uncertainty, retain uncertainty through partial information, distance, occlusion, competing possibilities, or explicit editorial disclosure.

Fantasy reconstruction may heighten scale, atmosphere, silhouettes, impossible geography, or symbolic energy only when its reconstruction status is editorially disclosed and it does not assert an unsupported historical fact.

characters: Recurring people retain locked identity, period logic, silhouette grammar, and scale role across scenes.
Pose, weather, injury, dirt, and local action may change without overwriting identity.
locations: Recurring locations preserve architecture, geography, landmark relationships, material logic, and a motivated spatial path across cuts.
Adjacent scenes must differ through approved terrain, weather, light, camera elevation, colour accent, screen direction, or human activity; novelty alone is not a reason to change location.
props: Recurring or historically meaningful props retain recognizable shape, material, scale, wear, ownership, and function.
No prop may silently become a new identity, inscription, heraldry, or historical claim between shots.

color: Derive colour from place, weather, time, material, and story state; do not let a generic golden sunrise or fixed palette replace scene-specific direction.
Use controlled warm/cool contrast only when motivated by the approved scene.
lighting: Use motivated natural, practical, architectural, fire, candle, moon, storm, or overcast light.
Do not default to spectacle sunbeams, heroic rim light, or identical dramatic skies across adjacent scenes.
material: Keep stone, wood, metal, soil, vegetation, textiles, water, and weathering physically legible.
Avoid glossy game-render surfaces, unsupported luxury, and decorative detail that invents historical certainty.

reconstructionEvidenceDistinction: Evidence and generated reconstruction remain visually and editorially distinct.
Generated readable text, pseudo-writing, maps, labels, unsupported heraldry, and fabricated inscriptions are forbidden unless a verified source asset—not a generated image—supplies them.
Use object silhouette, material, light, absence, and spatial context rather than invented writing to convey evidence or uncertainty.
compositionAndCameraTendencies: Favor environment-first wide and medium frames that establish danger, scale, geography, and human relationships before detail.
Make people or environmental forces act: approach, search, wait, flee, confront, gather, hide, discover, or react.
Use detail shots briefly to intensify touch, weight, danger, choice, or revelation; never let teeth, bone, diagrams, or display furniture replace the story.
An I2V keyframe contains separable foreground, action plane, and distant world; a clear travel or reveal corridor; complete bodies and props; credible contact; and a usable end-state handoff.
Vary shot scale, angle, motion function, and visual center across adjacent scenes while preserving identity and screen direction.
historicalUncertaintyHandling: Differentiate fact, reconstruction, hypothesis, legend, and unknown through the approved factual constraints.
Do not invent exact faces, inscriptions, colours, insignia, layouts, object details, or decisive outcomes beyond approved evidence.
When a high-energy fantasy image is used for legend or reconstruction, preserve its non-documentary status through editorial disclosure.
formatAdaptationRules: The same Visual Bible governs LONGFORM and SHORTFORM; format profiles own dimensions, safe areas, subtitle envelope, and delivery.
SHORTFORM keeps decisive faces, evidence, action contacts, and handoff anchors in the protected central story area; peripheral zones carry only lower-detail atmosphere or texture.
LONGFORM is horizontal 16:9, sustains geography and identity across sequences, and introduces a new question, discovery, danger, reversal, or payoff every 20 to 40 seconds.
LONGFORM uses shot-scale and camera-function variation; repeated static explanatory images or identical close-ups are not acceptable continuity.
avoidances: Do not inherit a project-specific palette, master image, character identity, or franchise style into the channel-wide resource.
Do not imitate Dragon Ball or any other identifiable franchise, character, logo, costume, pose system, or signature image language.
Avoid anachronisms, text artifacts, watermarks, UI, generic repeated golden-valley/castle vistas, unexplained heroic close-ups, cropped bodies, oversized foreground limbs, and disconnected props.
Avoid prolonged teeth, bone, artifact, diagram, genealogy, label, museum-support, or editorial-panel close-ups that turn the story into a lecture.
Avoid static figures posed only to illustrate narration, repeated camera moves, and scenes without a visible verb.
Avoid literal magical disappearance, physical-to-diagram morphs, and fantasy spectacle that can be mistaken for historical fact.
Avoid narration, dialogue, speech, voice, vocalization, or music in generated video clips; allow only restrained visible-action-supported ambience and effects.

visualDirectionGrammar.coreStatement: Story-first historical or disclosed-fantasy reconstruction: a still image is the first stable frame of a future video clip, not a standalone poster.

closeUpPolicy.rule: A close-up must have narrative purpose and remain safe for the planned video motion.

keyframeGrammar.motionVectorRule: Show one clear continuable vector: travel, weather drift, banner/cloth movement, force/action direction, atmospheric flow, or deliberate stillness.
keyframeGrammar.physicalIntegrityRule: People, animals, props, hands, weapons, and structures are complete, naturally connected, and not edge-clipped.

fantasyEnergyGrammar.allowed: For approved LEGEND or disclosed RECONSTRUCTION, use strong directional force, dynamic diagonals, readable action silhouettes, scale contrast, heightened atmosphere, and controlled energy effects.
fantasyEnergyGrammar.rule: Use the clarity and momentum associated with high-energy animation without copying any identifiable franchise.

handoffGrammar.rule: Each image leaves usable information for the next shot and I2V.

LONGFORM.rule: Favor continuity, geography, editability, and variation.

SHORTFORM.rule: Keep decisive action and handoff anchors in the central band.

tenExpertAcceptanceGate: Narrative director: one clear action and next-cut handoff.
Cinematographer: motivated unique camera and light.
Historical or role designer: correct collective silhouette grammar.
Motion designer: separable layers and one vector.
I2V supervisor: complete anatomy, props, contact, and safe scale.
Art director: approved finish without repeated generic defaults.
Editorial designer: no generated text, maps, labels, or overlays.
Continuity editor: required visual handoff survives the cut.

principles: Keep prompts compact; detailed design logic belongs upstream.
State narrative role, environment, video-ready keyframe requirements, and decisive avoidances before beauty language.
Carry only handoff constraints that materially affect the frame.

entertainmentDirection.audiencePromise: Give a general viewer an easy-to-follow historical mystery with curiosity, tension, surprise, and human consequence rather than an academic lecture or prolonged artifact inspection.
entertainmentDirection.informationBudget: Retain only three to five facts essential to the mystery; every visual fact must support an action, question, reveal, reversal, or payoff.
entertainmentDirection.openingRule: Within the first five seconds, make at least one place, action, anomaly, danger, or question visually legible.
entertainmentDirection.sceneRule: Every scene contains a visible verb performed by a person, group, animal, object, or environment and a designed handoff into the next scene.

allowedLevels.F0_RECORD: Use only when primary evidence itself must be inspected.
allowedLevels.F1_ATMOSPHERIC: Heighten weather, light, texture, and depth without changing factual meaning.
allowedLevels.F2_DRAMATIC_RECONSTRUCTION: Default: animated human action, cinematic depth, expressive silhouettes, motivated camera, and emotionally heightened natural phenomena.
allowedLevels.F3_SYMBOLIC_TRANSITION: Use briefly for mystery, memory, time, hypothesis, reveal, or scene transition while retaining editorial clarity.

stylizationGrammar.factBoundary: Stylization may intensify emotion and motion but cannot authenticate an unknown face, relationship, event, inscription, map, genealogy, or outcome.

characters.rule: Recurring characters must be identifiable by at least two locked features without depending on face close-ups.

locations.rule: A location is an action space with stable geography, not a decorative background.

props.rule: A prop earns screen time through action or a mystery question; full form and spatial relation precede any detail insert.

closeUpPolicy.artifactRule: Teeth, bone, documents, diagrams, labels, and specimens cannot become the long-duration visual protagonist.

temporalAndAudioGrammar.motionRule: Use natural but decisive acceleration; reach the edit target early enough to hold it. Camera, subject, and environment motions must have separate purposes.
temporalAndAudioGrammar.providerIndependence: Specify total generated duration, edit-use interval, target-arrival time, and hold independently of provider name or duration controls.

generatedAudio.mixRule: Keep generated ambience and effects separable from video, on A2, ducked beneath segmented narration.

stageGateContract.rule: A score below threshold blocks advancement. A fatal failure cannot be offset by points.
